newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold down amid talks of central bank selling.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold down amid talks of central bank selling.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures slipped across the board on Thursday, pressured by the yen's firmer tone, while bullion dipped amid a rumour that some central banks were involved in selling gold, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from two to seven yen per gram lower, with benchmark October down seven yen at 1,323 yen.

"Rumours of gold sales by some central banks surfaced during Asian hours, as some U.S. investment banks which are doing business with European central banks sold a large amount of gold in the spot gold market earlier in the day," one trading house trader said.
Spot gold was quoted at $369.30/60 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $370.70/371.20 in New York on Wednesday.
Although talk of central bank selling triggered fears that European central banks will sell more gold, the market was eyeing the U.S. stock market.

"Although the fundamental sentiment remains bearish, near-term direction hinges on the U.S. stock market," one trader said. "If U.S. stock prices continue to dip, investment funds are likely to cover their shorts," he said.
In the gold futures market, bargain-hunting buying was overwhelmed by active selling by trade houses, they said.
Silver and palladium futures ended mostly up, buoyed by firmer spot prices, but gains were stalled later amid uncertainity over the direction of the currency market.

Platinum futures settled narrowly mixed as private investors' long-liquidation was countered by bargain-hunting buying. One trader said constant bargain-hunting interest could ebb when the yen's further fall proves to be limited.
Benchmark October palladium ended up two yen per gram at 423 yen. Benchmark October silver was 0.3 yen per 10 grams lower at 176.6 yen. Benchmark October platinum was flat at 1,353 yen.
